name: StageList
description: Places entries by the lifecycle stage they belong to, so a reader at any stage finds what applies now. Five layouts over one data model: sheet, rail, index, checklist and cards.

keyboard: Tab moves through the index links and the checklist tick boxes in reading order; the other layouts hold no controls.
Space toggles the focused tick box; Enter follows the focused index link to its entry.
ariaRequirements: Phase and stage names are real headings, one level apart, starting at headingLevel so the list slots into the page outline.
The rail is an ordered list of stages; entries are list items.
The index overview is a navigation landmark named by indexLabel; each entry is an article named by its heading.
Each checklist stage is a fieldset named by its legend; each tick box is named by the entry's lead and described by the entry's detail.
The checklist count is a polite live region so ticking announces progress without moving focus.
Recurring stages are written out in text ("Again at ..."), never conveyed by position or colour alone.
a11y.reviewedNote: 2026-10-16: built from the format study for "Who to call and when" (Plausible Accessibility). Reviewed: heading levels and outline per variant, list semantics, index landmark and anchor targets, fieldset/legend grouping and checkbox names in the checklist, live-region count, keyboard path (Tab, Space, Enter) via play functions, light and dark themes, forced colours (rail markers and rules use CanvasText), 390px width with no horizontal overflow, axe clean per variant in unit tests. Known limitations: the sheet's pinned stage label assumes a sticky site header and reads --stage-list-sticky-offset; the checklist reads Checkbox's helper text by its id suffix (-helper) to mute it.

items.description: Entries to place by stage; each sits under the first stage it lists.

phases.description: Groups consecutive stages into phases for the sheet, checklist and cards layouts.

headingLevel.description: Level of the top headings the list renders.

storageKey.description: Checklist only: localStorage key that keeps ticks between visits.

indexLabel.description: Accessible name for the index layout's overview navigation.

className.description: Additional className for the root element.

forbiddenUse: Use for a sequence the reader must follow step by step to finish a task; that is a stepper or an ordered list of instructions.
Use when entries have no stage; a plain List or Table reads better.
dense: Entries placed by lifecycle stage (sheet, rail, index, checklist, cards); items name a lead answer, detail, stages and an optional tag

usage.description: StageList answers "what applies at this stage?". Each entry names its stages; the list places it under the first and writes out the later ones. Pick a layout for the reading task: sheet for scanning answers by stage (the default), rail when the order is the point, index for a long list read in two passes, checklist when the reader works through it on a project, cards for a looser overview.

bestPractices.description: Lead each entry with the answer the reader scans for (who to call, what to do) and keep the title as the smaller line.
Group more than about five stages into phases so the list has a short outline.
Set headingLevel to one below the surrounding section heading.
Give each stage a phrase for the recurrence line when its label would read oddly mid-sentence.
Do not use the checklist layout for state that must persist across devices or people; ticks stay in one browser.
Do not encode stage or recurrence with colour or position alone; the text says it.
